overview: Porth Nanven sits at the bottom of the Cot Valley, half a mile west of St Just, and it’s unlike any other beach in Cornwall. Instead of sand, the shore is covered in smooth, oval granite boulders, from hen’s-egg size to a metre or more across, which is why the media sometimes call it ‘Dinosaur Egg Beach’.
Look back at the cliff and you’ll see a whole wall of the same rounded boulders: an ancient beach from around 120,000 years ago, left stranded above today’s shoreline as sea levels changed.

expect.title: The ‘dinosaur eggs’
expect.text: Rounded boulders cover the beach; they’re protected, so please leave them where they are.

expect.title: The raised beach
expect.text: An old beach is preserved in the cliff behind, a rare sight.

expect.title: Cot Valley
expect.text: The walk down the wooded valley to the cove is lovely in its own right.

goodToKnow.label: Protected stones
goodToKnow.text: The National Trust owns the beach and the boulders are legally protected, so don’t take any home.

goodToKnow.label: Not for swimming
goodToKnow.text: It’s a rocky shore rather than a sandy beach.

week.text: A fascinating short stop on a day in the far west around St Just and Cape Cornwall. Combine it with a walk out to Cape Cornwall.

pairWith.why: a headland walk a kilometre or so north
a big sandy beach towards Sennen

tips: Go at sunset: it faces west and the light on the boulders is beautiful.
